To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) gestures can be classified using a context-dependent approach; 2) the classification of gestures is possible even if the gestures are not produced by a trained actor, as it happens in the case of spontaneous gestures produced during a conversation.

(1) the proposed approach is able to classify gestures using a small set of templates; (2) the proposed method performs better when it is trained with gestures produced by subjects of the same sex and age as the subjects of the test phase; (3) the proposed method is more effective if the training set includes a sufficient number of gesture repetitions; (4) the proposed method can be used in real-time gesture classification.

(i) the classification of hand gestures is possible by means of the kinematic and morphological parameters; (ii) the classification of the gestures is context-dependent, and (iii) the use of the context improves the classification accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the automatic classification of gestures, and it is based on the assumption that gestures are not only characterized by their kinematic properties, but also by their morphology, i.e., the shape of the hand configuration.
the development of a gesture recognition system based on the analysis of the kinematic characteristics and the morphology of hand gestures.

the automatic recognition of hand gestures in a context-dependent approach, and with the development of a system which is able to classify the gestures produced by a subject, using a small number of templates previously acquired during the learning phase of the procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the approach presented is able to classify gestures in a context-dependent way, and that it can be used as an effective tool for the automatic classification of hand gestures in a number of applications.
, in the context of the present study, the proposed classification approach is a promising solution to the problem of automatic gesture classification.
, by using a context-dependent approach, the classification of gesture sequences is possible with a good accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can classify the gesture types with a high degree of accuracy, by using as a reference a small subset of the total gestures produced by the users.

, in order to classify the gestures, we have developed an automatic system which is able to recognize and classify a large number of gestures, using a limited amount of data for each gesture class, and without the need of any a-priori knowledge on the subject.
we have developed a system that is capable to recognize a set of gesture classes, and that is able to adapt to different subjects and different contexts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a small number of templates, selected on the basis of their kinematic and morphologic characteristics, is a valid strategy to achieve a satisfactory classification performance.
, by exploiting a context-based approach, the number of gestures to be classified can be reduced to a manageable number, thus allowing for an effective and efficient gesture classification.

, when gestures have to be automatically classified, a context dependent approach is necessary to achieve good performance, and the kinematic characteristics of gestures are not sufficient to reach this objective.
